text:
Flitting through the forest understory, the crested quill displays an unusual pack hunting technique. With their spring-like legs, the 
small swarm synchronously launches themselves at flying birds, their sharp mandibles piercing hide and bringing down prey much 
larger than themselves. While descended from locusts, these insects do not amass in swarms thousands strong, but instead group 
together in swarms of their original spawning. Th ese spawn-kin spend most of their lives hunting together until they chance upon the 
spawn-kin of another, through an array of mesmerizing dances the two swarms will form and split, exchanging males to breed and 
propagate further swarms to patrol the Wealdwoods.

Encountering A lone crested quill and one living in a pack have 
two very different behaviors. When alone they act much like any 
other insect, mostly consisting on carrion and flitting away at 
the nearest disturbance. When in their spawning pack, a more 
cunning instinct overtakes them, and they act synchronously 
when flitting through the understory in search of a prey to 
ambush.
